## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 3, 4, 9) · ↓ invasive · Associated with lower invasive likelihood; spot check 0/20 [F2] · Unreliable
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 4, 9, 10) · context · Descriptive only; spot check 8/20 [F3] · Weak
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 1, 6, 9) · ↓ invasive · Associated with lower invasive likelihood; spot check 18/20 [F4] · Weak
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 3, 7, 11) · ↓ invasive · Associated with lower invasive likelihood; spot check 20/20 · Validated
- **Mean nuclear size 48 µm²** (regions 0, 2, 7) · context · Lowest in reference set; sampled regions only [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Deletion drop is 0.54 logits above random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so not shown to reflect classifier use; normal lobules (0/20) is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- The reliability flag reflects an atypical input, so probabilities may shift.
- Nuclei were measured in only 3 of 12 regions.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 6, 9**: confirm gland formation looks benign.
2. **Regions 3, 4, 9**: verify two-layered lobular epithelium by eye; the concept failed its spot check.
3. **Regions 7, 11**: look for stromal invasion or pleomorphism; these have the highest invasion and pleomorphism scores.
